hints: Focus on what actually happens when a Group 2 nitrate is heated, it forms the oxide plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.
Work out the moles of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ first using $M_r \approx 148.3$ and $29.7 \text{ g}$, you should get a very neat number.
Use the 2 to 1 mole ratio from the balanced equation to find moles of $\text{O}_2$, then multiply by 32 to get mass in grams.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced decomposition equation**

Remember, Group 2 nitrates always decompose the same way to oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. Write it down first so you get the ratio right.

$$2\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Calculate moles of magnesium nitrate used**

Moles is mass divided by $M_r$. This is the starting point for any reacting mass calculation.

$$M_r(\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2) = 24.3 + 2 \times (14.0 + 3 \times 16.0) = 148.3$$
$$n = \frac{29.7}{148.3} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$

**Use the mole ratio to find moles of oxygen**

Look at the equation. 2 moles of nitrate give only 1 mole of oxygen, so the ratio is 2 to 1.

$$n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.20 = 0.10 \text{ mol}$$

**Convert moles of oxygen to mass**

Now just multiply by the $M_r$ of $\text{O}_2$, which is 32.0.

$$m(\text{O}_2) = 0.10 \times 32.0 = 3.2 \text{ g}$$

options.A: Correct. 0.20 mol of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ produces half that amount, 0.10 mol, of $\text{O}_2$ because of the 2:1 ratio. $0.10 \times 32.0 = 3.2 \text{ g}$.
options.B: Incorrect. 6.4 g is exactly double the correct mass. This comes from using a 1:1 ratio and assuming 0.20 mol of nitrate gives 0.20 mol of $\text{O}_2$. Always check the balanced equation, it is 2 moles nitrate to 1 mole oxygen.
options.C: Incorrect. 12.8 g corresponds to 0.40 mol of $\text{O}_2$. This mistakes the coefficient of $\text{NO}_2$ (4) for oxygen, giving a 1:2 ratio. Oxygen has coefficient 1, not 2.
options.D: Incorrect. 19.2 g is far too large, about 0.60 mol of $\text{O}_2$. This often comes from not balancing the equation at all or confusing the mass of $\text{NO}_2$ plus $\text{O}_2$ with oxygen alone.
